description: Build a pure, DOM-free task-type engine that generates question specs for all new child-friendly task types, driven by the FEAT-002 content and the learner's age level. Task types: matching pairs (memory/match word-image), listen-and-choose (audio prompt + pick correct image/word), spell-the-word (build a word from letter tiles, no keyboard), true/false with an image, count-and-choose-the-number, and 'which matches' / find-a-color-in-a-scene. Also generate the classic 4-option multiple choice and English bidirectional translation (EN->PL and PL->EN) questions. Each generator returns a plain data spec (prompt, options, correct answer, and the underlying content item so the UI can record the answer via progressService). Keeping generation pure makes it unit-testable and keeps browser/audio concerns out of logic. Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: Create docs/js/logic/taskTypes.js (pure, DOM-free, no browser globals). Define a TASK_TYPES constant object with ids for each type: MULTIPLE_CHOICE, MATCH_PAIRS, LISTEN_CHOOSE, SPELL_WORD, TRUE_FALSE, COUNT_CHOOSE, WHICH_MATCHES (find-color-in-scene handled as a WHICH_MATCHES/find-color variant). Use string ids.

For each task type add a pure generator function that takes (item or items, pool of candidate items, options like optionCount, and a random function injected for determinism e.g. rng = Math.random) and returns a normalized question spec. Suggested spec shape: { type, moduleType, item (the primary content item used for recording), prompt (text/emoji/color to show), options (array of {id,label,emoji?,colorHex?,isCorrect}), correctItemId, meta (type-specific data e.g. tiles for SPELL_WORD, sentence for translation, sceneDescriptor for find-color) }. Reuse content builder fields; do not read the DOM.

MULTIPLE_CHOICE: current behavior as data (1 correct + N-1 distractors, shuffled). MATCH_PAIRS: produce N word-image pairs to match (data for a memory/match grid). LISTEN_CHOOSE: pick a target item plus distractors; meta indicates what to speak (use item.audioKey/prompt/answer and moduleType so the UI knows whether to speak Polish or English) and options are images/words to tap. SPELL_WORD: given a target word (English word or a Polish letter example word), produce the correct ordered letters plus a shuffled tile set (include a few distractor letters); expose a pure validator function isSpellingCorrect(tiles, target). TRUE_FALSE: pair an image/word with a statement that is either true or false (e.g. show emoji for 'cat' with label 'dog' -> false) and mark the expected boolean. COUNT_CHOOSE: given a count (0-9 or small number) produce that many object glyphs and number options to choose from. WHICH_MATCHES / find-color-in-a-scene: given a target (e.g. a color) and a scene set of candidates, mark which candidate matches.

Add English bidirectional translation generators (or a direction parameter on MULTIPLE_CHOICE/LISTEN_CHOOSE) so a question can ask EN->PL (show English, pick Polish) or PL->EN (show Polish, pick English), and support phrase/sentence kinds from FEAT-002.

Add a pure lesson-composition helper, e.g. buildLesson({ module, level, stage, availableItems, questionCount, taskTypeMix, rng }), that selects which task types are appropriate for the given age level (EARLY: simpler types with more images/audio, fewer text-heavy types; LATE: include SPELL_WORD, translation, sentences, harder mixes) and returns an ordered array of question specs. Keep it deterministic when rng is injected. Do NOT couple it to progressService or storage; it only consumes content + params.
Ensure generators degrade gracefully when a pool is too small (e.g. fewer distractors available) without throwing.

Add Vitest tests in tests/taskTypes.test.js using an injected deterministic rng (e.g. a seeded/sequence function) covering: each generator returns a well-formed spec with exactly one correct option and correct correctItemId; SPELL_WORD tiles contain all letters of the target and isSpellingCorrect validates correct vs incorrect orderings; TRUE_FALSE produces both true and false cases with the right expected boolean; COUNT_CHOOSE glyph count matches the number and the number is among options; translation direction switches prompt/answer sides correctly; buildLesson respects age level (EARLY excludes the harder types, LATE includes them) and returns questionCount specs; generators do not throw on tiny pools.
Run `npm test` and confirm all tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: docs/js/logic/taskTypes.js is pure (imports cleanly under Node, no DOM/browser globals) and exports TASK_TYPES plus a generator per task type and a buildLesson composer.
Each generator returns a normalized spec with a single correct option and a reference to the content item for answer recording.
SPELL_WORD provides shuffled tiles and a pure isSpellingCorrect validator; translation supports EN->PL and PL->EN.
buildLesson selects age-appropriate task types for EARLY vs LATE and is deterministic under an injected rng.
`npm test` passes including tests/taskTypes.test.js; existing tests still pass.
findings: Added docs/js/logic/taskTypes.js (pure, DOM-free): TASK_TYPES ids, DIRECTIONS, an injected-rng shuffle, generators for MULTIPLE_CHOICE (with EN<->PL direction, doubling as generateTranslation), MATCH_PAIRS, LISTEN_CHOOSE, SPELL_WORD (+ pure isSpellingCorrect validator), TRUE_FALSE (forceTruth for testing both cases), COUNT_CHOOSE, WHICH_MATCHES (incl. find-color-in-scene variant via colorLookup), plus taskTypesForLevel/TASK_TYPES_BY_LEVEL and a deterministic buildLesson composer (EARLY excludes SPELL_WORD; LATE adds it). All generators degrade gracefully on tiny/empty pools without throwing; all randomness is injected via rng (no Math.random, no DOM/audio/storage). tests/taskTypes.test.js adds 29 tests with a seq-based deterministic rng. npm test: 94 passed (65 existing + 29 new). No changes to existing files. Note: the LATE-includes-SPELL_WORD test uses a constant high rng () => 0.99 to steer type selection deterministically rather than a fragile hand-tuned sequence.
